assumptions: The distance measure chosen (Hamming, Levenshtein or sequence-Levenshtein) matches the error model of the platform.
limits: A guaranteed correction radius is a combinatorial property of the set, not a measured error rate.
Audits a set you have; design_barcodes makes one.
bio.jane/contract.question: What minimum distance does this index set have, how many errors does that correct, and which subset survives a stricter budget?

description: Check an index set you ALREADY have, rather than designing a new one: the minimum distance between any two, how many errors that guarantees correcting, the full distance matrices, and — optionally — the subset that survives pruning to a stricter error budget. This is the question asked of a set inherited from a kit or a previous experiment.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

metric.description: error model to audit against — a set safe under substitutions may be unsafe under indels. Values: hamming (Hamming (substitutions)), seqlev (Sequence-Levenshtein (indels)), levenshtein (Levenshtein).

prune_to_errors.description: also report the subset that would survive pruning to a free code correcting this many errors. 0 = do not prune. Advanced.

required_distance.description: the minimum distance the set is supposed to have — the audit says whether it does.

name: audit_barcodes

analysis.description: per-metric analysis of the whole set

audit.description: the verdict: the set's real minimum distance, what it guarantees, and every pair that falls short

baseComposition.description: the fraction of the set reading each base at each cycle

distanceHistogram.description: how many PAIRS sit at each distance under the chosen metric: the shape behind the minimum

distanceMap.description: the pairwise distance matrix under the chosen metric, as a heatmap

gcHistogram.description: how many barcodes sit at each GC percentage

kept.description: the barcodes surviving `prune_to_errors` (the whole set when pruning is off)

matrices.description: the pairwise distance matrix under each metric

neighbourHistogram.description: how many BARCODES have each nearest-neighbour distance: where the weak links are

statistics.description: the whole-set statistics the four charts above are drawn from, which a min-distance figure hides: GC mean, spread and range, Shannon entropy per cycle, the fraction reading each base at each cycle, groups sharing a prefix in the first cycles read, duplicates, and the per-metric distance distributions
